test_title: JSONPopulator #visit should throw an error for an unrecognized type
note: visit() dispatches on thing.isClassDeclaration()/isMapDeclaration()/isRelationship()/isTypeScalar()/isField(); the fallthrough throw only fires when none of those methods exist on `thing`. test_title: JSONPopulator #visitRelationshipDeclaration should get the relationship namespace if required
note: Only reachable by stubbing relationshipDeclaration.getFullyQualifiedTypeName() to return an unqualified name. Property#getFullyQualifiedTypeName() resolves through ModelFile#getFullyQualifiedTypeName(), which for any non-primitive type (a relationship target is never primitive) either resolves an import or a local declaration and always returns a namespace-qualified FQN; ModelUtil.getNamespace(typeFQN) therefore always finds a namespace and relationshipDeclaration.getNamespace() is never reached via the public API.

test_title: JSONPopulator #visitRelationshipDeclaration should not create a new relationship from an object if not permitted
JSONPopulator #visitRelationshipDeclaration should create a new relationship from an object if permitted
note: Verified against the reference: with acceptResourcesForRelationships:true, JSONPopulator does return the sub-Resource, but the outer assignment resourceObj.relAsset = subResource then runs through the outer resource's own live ValidatedResource property setter (Factory#newResource always builds a ValidatedResource unless options.disableValidation, which Serializer.fromJSON never sets). That setter's ResourceValidator is constructed bare (new ResourceValidator(), no permitResourcesForRelationships), so it rejects the Resource with a ValidationException ('...Expected a "Relationship"') before fromJSON can return. Confirmed by recording the scenario: the reference throws, it does not return a populated Resource as the W test (which uses a plain {} resourceStack with no live validation) asserts. Not reachable as a success outcome through the public API.
